student_learning_goal: I can represent any multiplication fact up to 10×10 as an array and find the related division.

header.student_learning_goal_banner: I can represent any multiplication fact up to 10×10 as an array and find the related division.
header.character_watermark: Maya in the top-right corner. Small (~1.5in tall).

parts.student_instructions: For each fact, write the array dimensions and the answer.
parts.visual_layout: Top of the page. Six tricky-fact array boxes in a 2x3 grid.

image_placeholders.description: Six fact array boxes in B&W line-art, 2-row × 3-column grid. Each ~2.2in × 1.8in. Pre-fills: 6×7, 7×8, 8×9, 9×6, 7×6, 8×7. Each box has 'rows × columns = ___' format.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS03_P1_SIX_TRICKY: keywords (array, tricky) name what the boxes ask for.

parts.student_instructions: Each problem shows a hint. Use the hint to find the related fact.

image_placeholders.description: Six rows in B&W line-art, stacked vertically. Each ~7in × 0.7in. Format: hint on left (e.g., '5×7=35'), arrow, target fact (e.g., '6×7=___'). Hints/targets: (5×7=35 → 6×7), (10×8=80 → 9×8), (5×6=30 → 7×6), (10×9=90 → 9×9), (5×8=40 → 7×8), (10×7=70 → 8×7).
image_placeholders.placement: Middle of the page; six rows.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS03_P2_HINTS: keywords (hint, derive) name what the rows ask for.

parts.student_instructions: Fill in the missing cells of the chart.
parts.visual_layout: Bottom of the page. A partial 10×10 multiplication chart.

image_placeholders.description: A partial 10×10 multiplication chart in B&W line-art, ~7in × 7in. Some cells filled in (the ×2, ×5, ×10 rows and columns plus a few others); ~30 cells blank for the child to fill.
image_placeholders.placement: Bottom of the page; full chart.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS03_P3_CHART: keywords (chart, multiplication) name what the page shows.

parts.answer_key: Standard 1-10 multiplication chart values. Children fill the ×3, ×4, ×6, ×7, ×8, ×9 rows.

parts.student_instructions: For each multiplication fact, write its inverse division facts: (a) 6×4 = 24; (b) 7×8 = 56; (c) 9×3 = 27.
parts.visual_layout: A 3-row table: each row has the multiplication fact on the left and two blank lines for inverse divisions on the right.

early_finisher_prompt: If you finish, find a fact in the chart that has a square answer (e.g., 4×4=16). List 3.
teacher_notes: Lesson 3 consolidation. Use Part 2 to assess distributive property fluency. Part 4 added to assess SC3 (related division) — verifies multiplication-division inverse fluency.
